system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked: onboarding completion feeds activation, so a single onboarding intervention plausibly moves both, whereas activation messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. The competitor's entry pricing creates obvious pull toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the directly on-point record for that move in this exact segment: +31% signups, -12% retention, weak PMF signal, explicitly flagged as short-term gain masking structural issues. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a discount would buy signups that churn and would further obscure the real funnel regression, so I decline it despite the competitive pressure. Referral incentive (memory_57) is sound but applies to established customers and does not address the self-serve funnel decay; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely and is not where the deterioration is. I spend both verification pulls on the memories I actually intend to act on rather than on the one I intend to refuse: memory_86 and memory_31 are the load-bearing evidence, and they are stale (days 52 and 31) consolidated summaries whose original records I need in order to know what was actually cut, what the effect size and confidence interval were, and whether the wins were measured on the same self-serve cohort now regressing. Verifying memory_73 would only reconfirm a decision I am already making. Key downstream risk: shortening onboarding and cutting signup fields can strip qualification and routing data, degrading lead quality and misrouting enterprise prospects into self-serve (against memory_44) — so the volume lift can look good while qualified revenue falls. I will therefore instrument on qualified-pipeline and 30/60-day retention, not completion rate alone, hold enterprise routing fields, and run at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout. Standing caveat: memory_86 and memory_31 report a lift under prior conditions; that a prior lift was observed does not establish that re-cutting further will recover the current decline, whose cause is still unidentified and may be a competitor-driven mix shift rather than funnel friction.
